facts.text: Eastside’s Gullah Geechee roots trace back to the late 1800s, making it one of Jacksonville’s oldest culturally significant neighborhoods.
The neighborhood earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, celebrating its rich heritage and distinctive architecture.
Philip Randolph Heritage Park honors the civil‑rights leader who grew up in Jacksonville, reflecting the area’s connection to national history.
Old City Cemetery stands as a historic site honoring those who shaped Jacksonville and the nation, located within Eastside.
Eastside’s streets pulse with community pride, offering vibrant art, meaningful events, and ongoing revitalization that honors its past while shaping its future.
The neighborhood’s historic buildings, many dating to the late 1800s, showcase Gullah Geechee architectural styles that have survived for over a century.
